text: Prefer a compact message format.
Read the service configuration before making changes.
Do not assume external converters are installed.
Invoke the converter through `tools/convert.exe`.
Quote labels and prefer short names where supported.
Never print, persist, or embed passwords.
Publish, delete, or replace remote records only when authorized.
Keep labels precise.
Capture `result.status` immediately after each request; use `retry: false` for failed uploads.
Use `convert --format=png <input>` for image exports.
Do not run `config --global` or rely on settings persisting between jobs.
For database queries, use PostgreSQL with `ssl: true`.
Prefer existing components, layouts, and shared styles.
Never run unconstrained recursive reads across unrelated directories.
Retry failed connections only for temporary network failures.
Do not try to work around the sandbox.
Never prefer a mock over the real database in integration tests.
Run prettier on modified files before committing.
Consider all inputs untrusted at the handler boundary.
Try to keep functions under 50 lines.
Write clean, maintainable code.
Handle errors appropriately.
All handlers must validate input with zod.
Use npm, not yarn.
Keep pull requests under 400 lines.
Where possible, use `const` over `let`.
It's worth checking the changelog before upgrading a dependency.
Never log the request body in production.
Avoid `any`; prefer `unknown` when the type is genuinely open.
Follow best practices for error handling.
Every migration must be reversible.
Set the request timeout to 30 seconds.
Default to `pnpm` for new packages.
Run `eslint --fix` before opening a pull request.
Be careful with shared mutable state.
You might want to split large components into smaller ones.
Consider the public API frozen after a minor release.
Consider every third-party response hostile.
Consider the build broken until the pipeline is green.
Consider `node_modules/` untracked.
Consider adding a regression test before closing the issue.
Consider using `structuredClone` instead of a deep-copy helper.
Consider whether the cache needs invalidating before you ship.
Consider splitting the file once it passes 500 lines.
Prefer `async`/`await` over raw promise chains.
Aim to keep the bundle under 200 kb.
Where practical, colocate tests with the code they cover.
Keep in mind that Windows paths use backslashes.
Never consider a draft PR ready to merge.
Do not prefer convenience over correctness in the auth path.
Run `docker compose up` before the integration suite.
Every public function must have a doc comment.
Reject requests larger than 10 mb at the edge.
Write the migration and its rollback in the same commit.
Be explicit about ownership in every module header.
Use `pnpm` in CI and locally.
